# Patch: Stinkyscape S13, spells on existing primitives

Closes #1867. Fills the 19 Stinkyscape S13 stubs behind R1420's gate (`#1` Freeze Ray, `#8` Conjure Rosemary Triscuit, `#8.1` Rosemary Triscuit, `#10–#12` Otherworldlies plus their nine spells, `#21` Moonberry, `#145` Fortify Flesh, `#146` Flash Freeze, `#156` Catalyst Comet) with scripts built only from engine verbs and prelude reads, plus one engine verb extension (`ShuffleCardIntoArgs.player` for Psychic Scream) and eleven rulings R1867000–R1867010 from this issue's block. No catalog, patch, doc, gate, or golden-trace change; shipped totals unchanged.

## Pass 2 (this pass)

**Review finding — HELD and fixed.** The reviewer was right: pass 1 added `player: Option<PlayerSpec>` to `ShuffleCardIntoArgs` in [shuffle_card.rs](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-1867/crates/engine/src/effects/shuffle_card.rs) but never regenerated the committed Luau typed module, whose `ShuffleCardIntoArgs` still listed only `instanceId`. Fixed by regenerating with `cargo test -p jackioh-luau --features ts --test export_api`, which produced exactly the expected one-line diff (`player: PlayerSpec?,`, matching every other optional-player arg in the file). Verified the finding's evidence first (`grep` showed the stale type at old line 2269), and checked for sibling staleness: `ShuffleCardInto` appears nowhere under `apps/web/src/wire/`, so no other generated artifact needed updating.

## How it was tested

- `cargo test -p jackioh-luau --features ts --test export_api` — passes; re-ran to confirm idempotent (second run green, no further diff).
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean.
- Pass 1's evidence stands: scoped card and engine suites green, `catalog check`, `patches check`, and `spec check` green (rerun of the one affected gate is what this pass changed).

- Regenerate rather than hand-edit the Luau module: it is generator-owned (`tests/export_api.rs` fails CI when a run changes it uncommitted), so the generator's output is the only honest fix — and it matched the reviewer's predicted rendering exactly.
- No scope widened: one generated line added, nothing refactored, no test touched (existing `export_api` test is the gate that covers it).

- `c156`: pool is the six shipped Catalyst cards over seeds (S #147 only under `preview_sets`); Comet ends in its owner's deck, in the graveyard if full; radiant card Radiant and Comet returns Radiant (`r1867010_…`).

## Done when

- All 19 scripts return effects built from engine verbs, read state only through the prelude, and their tests (base, Radiant, BUILD M12 row each) pass.
- `shuffle_card_into` carries the opponent-deck move with its engine test, proving R1867006 from both sides.

- The set is still gated: no `SHIPPED_SETS` edit, no pending fragment, no golden-trace move, shipped totals unchanged.
- `fmt`, `clippy`, the scoped card and engine tests, `catalog check`, `patches check`, and `spec check` are all green.

## Risks

- Ownership mid-resolution (Scream): setting `owner` on a field card before the library move could confuse views or generators; the engine test asserts the moved card's owner, zone, and later draw-as-owner, and `controller` is set alongside `owner` as `new_instance` does.
- Echo plus rng draws (Missiles): each re-resolution must draw among the still-standing; tests assert a killed unit is never drawn and the cursor advances exactly per hit.
- Adjacency reads (Freeze Ray, Frostbolt, Death/Pain): neighbours are read as the effect resolves, before the target leaves; tests pin lanes 1–3 plus a lone unit, and Death/Pain assert `required` refuses the play with no legal target.
- Hidden information: generated cards stay hidden per R97; tests assert opponent views where C+ #32's tests do.
- Determinism: every random choice goes through `ctx` rng with fixed seeds; tests pin seeds and never wall-clock.

## Open questions

- None blocking. One judgment call for review: eleven notes is many, but the foundation's `§8.10` note says each part's ST-S13 readings take R numbers from this issue's block, so one note per undecided reading is the faithful shape; if review finds any reading already decided by spec, that note should be dropped and its tests renamed to drop the `r` token.
